candidates.title: Paired signed vertical-gradient zero-crossing traces
candidates.physical_signature: Co-located, strike-continuous zero-crossing centerlines in magnetic and gravity vertical-gradient fields, with opposed-sign lobes on both sides; sign topology rather than high gradient magnitude is the target.
candidates.why_it_may_find_omitted_faults: A concealed fault may offset or juxtapose magnetized and density-contrasting basement units beneath basin fill without leaving a clear surface scarp; paired potential-field responses could reveal the boundary.
candidates.difference_from_repo_prior_art: H33-6 used raw TMI/gravity gradient magnitudes and edge-normal alignment with basement/conductivity corroboration. No active candidate builder implements the paired signed-zero-crossing operator; existing code has individual derivatives and coherence primitives.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contact, dike, or basin-fill boundary can generate paired magnetic/gravity lobes without fault displacement.
candidates.expected_improvement: Qualitative priority 1 of 3; moderate plausible upside; no numeric DTI prediction.
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; requires label-blind scale rules, per-feature leakage canaries, fold-safe comparison, and matched-count control.
candidates.data_availability: Requires the official competition GeoDAWN feature raster; it is not staged in this checkout. Owner-mirror input pins do not authenticate organizer provenance.
